question: How many days of annual leave do full-time employees get?
expected_answer: 28 days a year, including bank holidays (more with long service, up to 30).
ai_answer: Full-time employees get 28 days of paid annual leave each leave year, including bank holidays. Under the current Annual Leave Policy (v2026.1), long-service days are added: 29 days after 3 years' continuous service and 30 days after 5 years, with a maximum entitlement of 30 days. Part-time employees receive a pro-rata entitlement. Note that the older Annual Leave Policy (v2024.1) gave 1 extra day (29 days in total) after 5 years' service, which conflicts with the 2026.1 figures and has been superseded by it.

question: When do we get paid?
expected_answer: Monthly, on the last working day of the month.
ai_answer: Employees are paid monthly on the last working day of the month, according to Employee Handbook §5 Pay (P1). Payslips are available in StaffHub. The passages do not cover any other pay timing details.

question: How long is the probation period for new starters?
expected_answer: 6 months, with reviews at 3 and 6 months; can be extended by up to 3 months.
ai_answer: New employees have a 6-month probation period, with review meetings held by their manager at 3 months and 6 months. Probation may be extended by up to 3 months if more time is needed. During probation, the notice period on either side is 1 week.

question: What is the mileage rate if I use my own car for work?
expected_answer: 45p per mile (normal commuting can't be claimed).
ai_answer: Mileage in a personal car is paid at 45p per mile under the Expenses Policy (v2025.1, §3 Travel). Normal commuting to your usual workplace cannot be claimed.

question: How long does my password need to be?
expected_answer: At least 14 characters, with MFA wherever supported.
ai_answer: Passwords must be at least 14 characters long, as set out in section 4 of the Information Security Policy (v2025.1). The IT Acceptable Use Policy (section 7) confirms employees must follow these same password rules.

question: How quickly must a customer complaint be acknowledged?
expected_answer: Within 2 working days (final response within 8 weeks).
ai_answer: A customer complaint must be acknowledged within 2 working days. The final response must be sent within 8 weeks.

question: How much company sick pay do I get if I've worked here for 4 years?
expected_answer: 4 weeks at full pay in any rolling 12 months (after probation), on top of SSP.
ai_answer: If you have between 3 and 5 years' length of service and have completed probation, you get 4 weeks of company sick pay at full pay in any rolling 12-month period. Company sick pay tops up SSP to full basic pay.

question: What support can I get for studying a qualification?
expected_answer: Course fees up to £1,000 a year and up to 5 days' paid study leave, after probation.
ai_answer: Employees who have passed probation can apply for study support for a qualification relevant to their role. It covers course fees of up to £1,000 per year and up to 5 days of paid study leave per year for exams and study. Applications are made through LearnHub and must be approved by the line manager and the Head of Learning and Development. If you leave within 12 months of a course finishing you must repay 100% of the course fees, and if you leave 12 to 24 months after it finishes you must repay 50%.

question: If I leave 18 months after the company paid for my course, do I have to pay anything back?
expected_answer: Yes, 50% of the course fees (leaving between 12 and 24 months after the course).
ai_answer: Yes. Under the Training and Development Policy, if you leave between 12 and 24 months after the course finishes, you must repay 50% of the course fees. Leaving 18 months after the course ends falls in this range, so you would repay 50%. The passages do not state the exact fee amount to be repaid or how the repayment is collected.

question: Is there an allowance for working from home?
expected_answer: £26 a month for employees contracted to work remotely at least 1 day a week.
ai_answer: Yes. Employees whose contract says they work remotely at least 1 day a week receive a home working allowance of £26 a month, paid through payroll. The passages do not say whether employees who work from home without this in their contract qualify for the allowance.

question: Can I roll over unused holiday into next year?
expected_answer: Yes, up to 8 days, which must be used by 30 June.
ai_answer: Yes. Under the current Annual Leave Policy (v2026.1, effective 1 January 2026), you can carry forward up to 8 days of unused annual leave into the next leave year (1 January to 31 December). The carried-forward days must be used by 30 June of the new leave year, or they are lost and not paid. You do not need approval for up to 8 days, and the carried-forward days appear automatically in StaffHub from 2 January. The older 2024 version of the policy (5 days, deadline 31 March, approval needed by 1 December) has been superseded, so it does not apply. The passages do not say how this applies to casual or zero-hours workers' accrued holiday.

question: I clicked a dodgy link in an email. What should I do?
expected_answer: Report it to the IT Service Desk immediately (and use Report Phish for suspicious emails).
ai_answer: If you have already clicked a link or entered your password, report it to the IT Service Desk immediately. You should also report the suspicious email using the Report Phish button in Outlook, and do not click links or open attachments in suspicious emails. The IT Service Desk can be contacted through StaffHub or on extension 4357.

question: Can I keep the tips a punter gives me at the blackjack table?
expected_answer: No. Gaming staff tips go in the tronc box and are shared through the tronc scheme.
ai_answer: No. Gaming employees must never keep tips personally. All tips given to gaming employees go into the tronc box at the table and are shared through the tronc scheme (Code of Conduct §3). Hospitality employees follow their venue's tipping process instead.

question: I'm too poorly to work my shift on the casino floor. How early do I need to ring in?
expected_answer: At least 2 hours before the shift starts, by phone to the line manager or duty manager.
ai_answer: Gaming floor, security and cage employees must phone their line manager or the duty manager at least 2 hours before the start of their shift, so cover can be arranged (Sickness Absence Policy §2). Do not text or email unless you cannot speak. You must call again each day you are absent unless your manager agrees otherwise or you have a fit note.

question: How quickly do I have to report a lost company laptop?
expected_answer: Immediately, and in any case within 1 hour, to the IT Service Desk.
ai_answer: A lost or stolen company device, including a laptop, must be reported to the IT Service Desk immediately, and in any case within 1 hour of noticing it is missing. Reporting quickly allows the device to be wiped remotely.

question: What happens to my annual leave if I'm ill while I'm on holiday?
expected_answer: With a fit note, those days count as sickness and the leave is given back. Report it on day one.
ai_answer: If you are ill during booked annual leave and provide a fit note covering the days of sickness, those days are treated as sickness absence and your annual leave is returned to you. You must report the sickness on the first day, following section 2 of the Sickness Absence Policy.

question: Where do I report a customer I think is laundering money?
expected_answer: Directly to the MLRO with the internal suspicious activity report form, not SafeLog; never tell the customer.
ai_answer: Do not report suspected money laundering in SafeLog, and do not discuss it with the customer or with colleagues who do not need to know. Complete the internal suspicious activity report form and send it directly to the Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) on the same day, as described in the Compliance Guidelines. Do not investigate yourself, and do not tell the customer, as tipping off is a criminal offence.

question: Can I claim my course fees back on expenses?
expected_answer: No. Course fees are paid directly by the company under the Training Policy.
ai_answer: No. Course fees cannot be claimed on expenses. They are paid directly by the company under the Training and Development Policy (P1, and P2 confirms training course fees cannot be claimed). Travel and accommodation for approved training can be claimed under the Expenses Policy instead.

question: Someone on the gaming floor looks under 18. What do I do?
expected_answer: Ask for photo ID (Think 25), tell the duty manager immediately, and log it before the end of the shift.
ai_answer: Nobody under 18 may enter the gaming floor, and anyone who appears to be under 25 must show valid photo ID under Think 25. The passages do not set out the specific steps to take when someone who looks under 18 is already on the floor, such as who to inform or how to remove them, so check with your duty manager or follow your usual escalation process.

question: I was off sick for months last year and couldn't use my leave. How much can I carry over and by when?
expected_answer: Up to 20 days because of long-term sickness, to be used within 18 months of the end of that leave year.
ai_answer: Because you were off with long-term sickness, the exception in the current Annual Leave Policy (v2026.1, §8) applies: you may carry forward up to 20 days instead of the usual 8. Days carried forward because of sickness must be used within 18 months of the end of the leave year in which they were earned. Other exceptional carry-forward must be used by 30 June. The passages do not say how the carry-forward is approved for sickness cases; the older v2024.1 policy (P4) says exceptions for long-term sickness must be approved by the Head of HR, but it is superseded by v2026.1 and the passages do not confirm whether that approval step still applies. Please confirm the approval process and the exact deadline for your leave year with HR, as the passages do not set out how the 18-month period is counted from a specific date.

question: Can gaming floor staff take two weeks off over Christmas?
expected_answer: No. 24 Dec to 1 Jan is a peak period; at most 5 consecutive days, and only with the General Manager's approval.
ai_answer: Probably not. Under the current Annual Leave Policy (v2026.1, §7), 24 December to 1 January is a peak period, and gaming floor employees may take no more than 5 consecutive days of leave during peak periods, and only with approval from their venue's General Manager. Two weeks over Christmas would therefore exceed that limit. Leave is also requested through StaffHub with notice of at least twice the length of the leave (so 2 weeks of leave needs 4 weeks' notice, per v2026.1 §6), and requests after the rota is published (4 weeks in advance) can only be approved if cover is available. Note that the older v2024.1 policy (§6) says leave between 20 December and 2 January is not normally approved for gaming floor employees, which is a different rule; the passages do not say which applies beyond the v2026.1 version being the later one.

question: How much notice do I need to give to book a week of annual leave?
expected_answer: Twice the length of the leave, so 10 days for 5 days of leave; later if the rota is already published.
ai_answer: Under the current Annual Leave Policy (v2026.1, effective 1 Jan 2026), leave must be requested through StaffHub with notice of at least twice the length of the leave. For a week of leave (5 working days), that means at least 10 days' notice before the first day of leave. Gaming floor and security rotas are published 4 weeks in advance, and requests made after a rota is published can only be approved if cover is available. Managers should respond within 5 working days. Note that the older policy version (v2024.1) in P1 does not address booking notice, and P2 is the version to rely on.

question: How much annual leave can I carry forward?
expected_answer: Up to 8 days, used by 30 June (the 2024 rule of 5 days by 31 March no longer applies).
ai_answer: Under the current Annual Leave Policy (v2026.1, effective 1 Jan 2026), you can carry forward up to 8 days of unused annual leave into the next leave year without needing approval, and these days appear automatically in StaffHub from 2 January. Sickness-related days must be used within 18 months of the end of the leave year in which they were earned, while other exceptional days must be used by 30 June. The older v2024.1 policy (P1) allowed 5 days with a 31 March deadline and a request to your manager before 1 December, but it has been superseded by v2026.1.

question: How many days a week can office staff work from home?
expected_answer: Up to 2 days with manager agreement; Tuesday and Wednesday are office days (not 3, as in 2023).
